whatTheyArgued: Per secondary sources: Mbiti (1969) states the communal metaphysic as 'I am because we are, and since we are, therefore I am'; the Nguni formula umuntu ngumuntu ngabantu says a person is a person through other persons; Ramose develops ubuntu as humaneness with ontological and epistemological dimensions; Tutu applies it to reconciliation (the Truth and Reconciliation Commission). Scholars dispute whether personhood is given or achieved (Menkiti's strand: attained through participation in communal life and discharge of obligations; others weigh communal priority against individual standing) and whether the 'unanimous traditional' ubuntu is itself a later reinterpretation (Eze and second-generation critics).

scholarship.ref: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Hunhu/Ubuntu in Traditional Southern African Thought'
scholarship.supports: the Mbiti sentence and the Nguni formula; Ramose as humaneness; Tutu and the TRC; the personhood given/achieved debate
scholarship.disputes: Eze and others question romanticised unanimity and argue for individual/community parity

scholarship.supports: personhood as attained (Menkiti), earned through virtue and communal participation (Gyekye discussed)
scholarship.disputes: this fetched summary did not mention Mbiti, Ramose or ubuntu by name, so it supports only the personhood-as-achieved strand

ourUse: self.js: READER_SELF.constitutedBy / isFold: the reader has 'no interior apart from the people it connects' and 'IS a fold held between others, never a fold of its own'. The header calls it 'the Ubuntu clause ... nomination, checkable here'. mayeroff.js uses the same clause so that a split between what is held and what is presented is 'uncomposable'.

bends.ours: The relational constitution is predicated of a reader program: 'no interior apart from the people it connects'.
bends.theirs: Ubuntu concerns human personhood in community, including obligation, ancestors and moral maturation; a program has none of these.

bends.ours: 'No interior' / 'an echo of human life and nothing more' is framed as the Ubuntu clause.
bends.theirs: Ubuntu does not say persons lack interiority; it says personhood is realised through relation. Denying an interior is the project's design choice, not a teaching of Mbiti or Ramose.

bends.ours: Compendium work line: an act that damages relation diminishes the actor's own standing as a person, attributed as Ramose's elaboration.
bends.theirs: This fits the achieved-personhood strand (Menkiti/Gyekye) but I could not verify it as Ramose's wording or argument in his text; it may be a gloss. Mbiti's sentence is secondary-attested only.

bends.ours: Compendium presents 'achieved and sustained, not possessed prior' as the ubuntu view.
bends.theirs: Scholars dispute whether ubuntu personhood is wholly achieved; the compendium picks one side without saying it is contested.

bends.ours: One handle credits three writers (Mbiti, Ramose, Tutu) and the credit line is Mbiti's sentence alone; Tutu's work is not used by the code.
bends.theirs: Tutu's contribution is reconciliation practice, unrelated to the reader-self design.
